name: Church HQ
verified: 2026-11-08 · Church HQ · driven end to end at 390×844, empty storage, no key
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this page has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the page already has a church's details in it, go back to your list and tap this app's name again rather than using a bookmark or your history.

THIS TEST IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHERS. You are not checking that buttons work. You are pretending to be somebody who has just BOUGHT this, has nobody to help them, and has to get their church's own details into it from nothing.

WHAT THIS PAGE IS, so you are not surprised at the end: it is where a church types in everything about itself — its name, times, address, this week's news, its staff. It then hands you a file to pass on to whoever looks after the church's app. It does not build the app itself. If you reach the end expecting a finished church app and do not get one, that is the page working as intended, not a fault.

So: do not look anything up, and do not ask anybody. If you get stuck, that is the most useful thing you can tell us — say exactly where you stopped and what you expected to happen. A step you could not finish is worth more to us than a step you forced your way through.

Pretend you are the church secretary at Grace Chapel in Nakuru. Sunday services are at 9am and 11am, you are at 12 Kenyatta Avenue, the office phone is 0712 345678, and this Sunday there is a harambee after the service for the new roof.

steps.do: Open the page. Do not tap anything yet — just read the top of the screen.
steps.see: A line near the top says “Not ready to publish yet. Still needed: church name, service times, address.” Below it, “What this is”, and a yellow button “Start with the basics →”.
steps.tip: That line is the page telling you what it still wants. Watch it as you go — it changes.

steps.do: Tap “Start with the basics →”.
steps.see: A screen headed “The basics”, with eight boxes down it: Church name, Service times, Address, Phone, Office email, Website, Giving link, and a YouTube one. Every box is EMPTY — the grey writing inside each is only an example of what goes there.
steps.tip: If any box already has real words in it that you did not type, that is a fault — say so.

steps.do: Tap the Church name box and type this.
steps.see: Your words are in the box, in normal dark writing rather than grey.

steps.do: Tap the Service times box and type this.
steps.see: Your words are in the box.

steps.do: Tap the Address box and type this.
steps.see: Your words are in the box.

steps.do: Scroll back to the very top of the page and read that line again.
steps.see: It no longer says anything is still needed. It now says “Ready to publish.”
steps.tip: This is the one thing in this test that tells you that you have done enough. If it still lists something as needed, go back and find the box it is naming.

steps.do: Tap the Phone box and type this.
steps.see: Your number is in the box.

steps.do: Leave the Website, Giving link and YouTube boxes completely empty. Scroll past them.
steps.see: Nothing complains. Nothing turns red. An empty box is allowed here.
steps.tip: A real small church often has none of these. If the page insists on them, that is a fault.

steps.do: At the bottom of the screen, tap “📣 News”.
steps.see: A screen headed “This week”, with a HEADLINE box and a THE DETAIL box, and under them “What’s coming up” which says nothing is dated yet.

steps.do: Tap the HEADLINE box and type this.
steps.see: Your words are in the box.

steps.do: Tap THE DETAIL box and type this.
steps.type: After the second service this Sunday. Bring what you can.
steps.see: Your words are in the box.

steps.do: Under “What’s coming up”, tap “✚ Add an event”.
steps.see: A row of empty boxes appears for the event, with a small ✕ beside it for removing it again. “Nothing dated yet.” is gone.
steps.tip: Fill the event in however you think it should be filled in. There is no right answer here — we want to see what you do.

steps.do: At the bottom, tap “👥 People”, then tap “✚ Add a person”.
steps.see: Boxes appear for NAME, TITLE and EMAIL OR PHONE, with “✕ remove” beside them.

steps.do: Put the pastor in: Daniel Kimani, Pastor, and the office phone 0712 345678.
steps.see: The three boxes hold what you typed.

steps.do: Lower down, tap “✚ Add a ministry” and put in a youth group however you think it should go.
steps.see: A row for the ministry appears and takes what you type.
steps.tip: Again, there is no right answer. If you cannot work out what it wants, say so — that is the finding.

steps.do: At the bottom, tap “📤 Publish”. Read the whole screen before tapping anything.
steps.see: It says “Ready to publish.” and “Nothing has gone out yet”. It also says “No mailbox set up yet — Publish will hand you the file to send by hand instead.” There are buttons including “📣 Publish to the congregation” and “👀 See what they will see”.

steps.do: Tap “👀 See what they will see”.
steps.see: A NEW TAB opens showing your church's own page: Grace Chapel Nakuru at the top, your service times, “Find us” and your address. At the bottom it says “This is what your congregation sees.”
steps.tip: If instead a box says your browser blocked the preview window, that is your phone stopping pop-ups, not a fault in the app. Allow pop-ups for this page and tap the button again. Tell us if it happened, though — a church secretary would not know what to do about that. Then read the page as though you were somebody in the pews: is anything missing that you typed in, or there that you did not?

steps.do: Close that tab and come back to Church HQ.
steps.see: You are back on the Publish screen.

steps.do: Tap “⬇ Save it as a file”.
steps.see: Your phone saves a file, and its name has your church's name in it — something like “grace-chapel-nakuru-app.json”.
steps.tip: If your phone asks where to put it, anywhere is fine. If nothing at all happens, that is a fault — say so.

steps.do: Tap “📣 Publish to the congregation”.
steps.see: A small box says there is no mailbox yet, so it has copied your church file instead, and tells you to paste it to whoever looks after your app. Tap through it.
steps.tip: Nothing is sent anywhere. There is no congregation — this is your test copy.

steps.do: Now pull the page down to reload it (or tap ↻ in your browser). Then tap “⛪ Basics”.
steps.see: Everything you typed is still there — the church name, the times, the address, the phone.

steps.do: THE REAL QUESTION. Think back over the whole thing and answer honestly in the box: if nobody had given you these steps, could you have filled this in on your own? Where would you have got stuck? And at the end, did you know what you were supposed to do with the file?
steps.see: There is no right answer and no wrong one. “I would not have known what to do at the Publish screen” and “I did not understand what the file was for” are exactly the kind of answers we need. This is going to be sold to church secretaries who will have nobody to ask.
steps.tip: This is the most valuable step in the test. Please do not skip it.

steps.do: Now the video. This app has 1. Open it and watch it right through, sound on: Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=churchhq
steps.see: The video plays with a voice, the screen inside it changes as the words change, and nothing it describes is missing from the app you just used. If the voice stops partway, or it talks about a button that is not there, say which.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees before they buy: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find this app and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The price says Free, with an optional donation to Loving InDeed. That is right: nothing is sold, and nobody has to give. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which part.
